correctness.rationale: All 128 binary words and every exact single-overwrite error ball are reconstructed by two distinct formulas. The first coordinate is unchanged and complement maps its two 64-word fibers bijectively. In one fiber, exact pivoted Bron--Kerbosch enumeration finds exactly one clique of size at least 13; an independent ordered backtracking enumeration with provably safe greedy-coloring bounds finds exactly one clique of size 13 and no clique of size 14. Their common unique clique is the explicitly displayed 13-word half. The 26-word complement union is independently checked for all pairwise disjoint balls. This proves both the upper bound and unique equality, with no unproved extrapolation.

originality.rationale: Sharov--Roth and Gabrys--Yaakobi--Dolecek explicitly cover the classical numerical optimum M(7,1)=26, which is excluded from the new contribution. Section IV of the former states uniqueness for other correction radii and infinity-grain codes, not for n=7,t=1. Neither fully inspected directly relevant source states the unique labeled 26-word extremizer or forces it from a general theorem; the finite equality classification is checked against published-record and own-prior findings under natural aliases.
residual_risks: An obscure or unindexed finite census may already list the same unique size-26 length-seven code.
The paper comparison distinguishes published uniqueness theorems by their quantifiers and radii; it does not certify absence from all unpublished supplementary sources.

value.rationale: The known sharp cardinality 26 is not the contribution. The new result is a natural complete equality classification at the canonical length-seven single-grain parameter in classical optimal-size tables: every maximum is forced to contain a particular 13-word branch and its complement, and it is unique even with physical coordinates labeled. This rigidity is substantive structural information beyond the bound and one construction, and is useful as a finite design benchmark in grain-channel coding.
